item.title: LORNA SHORE Releases 'Unbreakable' Single and Music Video: 'It Will Never Break Us Down'
item.description: Lorna Shore has dropped a new single, “Unbreakable”, along with a fresh music video, giving fans another preview of their next album, I Feel The Everblack Festering Within Me.

item.title: DAVID VINCENT Reflects On Fan Expectations: 'Nobody Cares About The New Stuff'
item.description: David Vincent, the former Morbid Angel frontman, isn’t exactly rushing to crank out new material with I Am Morbid. In a recent sit-down with Altars Of Metal, the inevitable question popped up: will I Am Morbid ever release original songs?

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Meshuggah Drops "Ligature Marks" Music Video Alongside "Immutable - The Indelible Edition" Announcement
item.description: Yep, MESHUGGAH is back to make your speakers beg for mercy—again. Not just playing their usual brand of mind-melting, time-signature-abusing, existential-crisis-inducing metal—oh no, they’ve decided to remaster their already ridiculous 2022 album Immutable and slap on a shiny new title: “Immutable - The Indelible Edition” (because clearly, “Immutable” wasn’t immutable enough).

item.title: Cradle Of Filth: Ashok Šmerda and Zoë Marie Federoff marry in a gothic ceremony
item.description: Two Cradle Of Filth bandmates just got hitched. (Yes, you read that right. And it’s almost too metal to handle.) Guitarist Marek “Ashok” Šmerda and keyboardist Zoë Marie Federoff promised forever this week, and Dani Filth celebrated by posting a barrage of wedding photos for the goths, the headbangers, and everyone in between.

item.title: Necrobutcher on Mayhem's Four Decades of Survival
item.description: When the bassist of your band murders the guitarist, you’d think the group might call it quits. Most bands implode over petty squabbles about songwriting credits or tour schedules—not criminal trials.

item.title: Andrés 'Hades' Adasme of Lucifer’s Hammer Dead at 38
item.description: Andrés “Hades” Adasme—a name that’s been synonymous with Lucifer’s Hammer since 2012. The voice. The energy. The force behind four blistering albums. Now, at just 38, he’s gone.
